subject: Operationalizing pilot: recap, success metrics, and next steps (OrchardAI)
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Greene <alyssa@orchardai.com>
Cc: Marcus Liu <marcus.liu@orchardai.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Operationalizing pilot: recap, success metrics, and next steps (OrchardAI)

Hi Alyssa / Marcus —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned before we kick off the pilot:  

Pain points you called out:
- Inconsistent latency on your current LLM endpoints during peak batch inference (esp. 200–500 reqs/min).
- High per-token costs causing model access to be throttled for lower-priority workflows.
- Lack of end-to-end observability: can’t track request-level cost/latency per model/route.

Pilot goals (30 days):
1) Demonstrate 30–50% reduction in per-token cost via batching + KV caching for the summarization pipeline.
2) Achieve median response latency <= 350 ms for single-turn summarization requests (95th perc target <= 700 ms).
3) Integrate token-level cost/latency dashboards and one alert for quality regressions on the prompt set.

Success criteria (what counts as a win):
- Clear cost delta in our console compared to your current baseline (we’ll compare the same traffic profile).
- End-to-end trace for a sample failure to demonstrate debugability.
- Security review checklist completed for data-in-flight and retention.

Next steps I propose (owners & timing):
- You: Share access to a non-prod dataset (S3 link or sample payloads) + expected QPS profile by Friday 12/11 (Alyssa, Marcus).
- Redwood: Send back our minimal access checklist and the initial mutual action plan by EOD 12/09 (Monica).
- Redwood Engineering: Stand up a dev pool and provide test endpoints + initial prompt set for eval within 72 hours of access (Karthik).
- Analytics: Build baseline eval dashboards and wire up one alert (Grace) — target demo on day 14.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short security questionnaire we usually start with and an editable mutual action plan.

Proposed pilot kickoff window: next Monday (12/14) or Tuesday (12/15) — 30–45 minute sync to confirm owners, cadence, and immediate blockers. Please confirm what works.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
m: (415) 555-0129

Hi Monica —

Thanks for the clear recap — that aligns with how we saw the conversation. A few clarifications:  
- The QPS profile is spiky: baseline 40–60 qps, bursts to ~480 qps for 10–15 minute intervals during peak ingestion.
- Our summarization pipeline payloads average 280 tokens input and we expect ~40 tokens output.

We’ll share a sanitized S3 bucket with representative payloads by EOD Friday (12/11). I’ll also put Marcus on the access/infra emails — he’ll be the technical lead from our side.

12/14 morning PT works for a kickoff; prefer 10am PT (we can do alternate time if you’re tight).

One question: will the pilot run in your hosted environment or will we run a private VPC deployment? For the first 30 days we prefer hosted but need assurances on token retention and a short-term retention policy.

Best,
Alyssa Greene
Head of ML Products | OrchardAI
alyssa@orchardai.com

Thanks Alyssa — good notes. Quick follow-up from our side:  

1) Pilot environment: we can run the 30-day pilot in our hosted environment with a short-term retention override (30 days) — that meets your ask and accelerates setup. I’ve noted this as a requirement in the MAP.

2) Access checklist: attached is the minimal set we need (IAM user, temp S3 read access, sample payloads). Please don’t share production credentials — a sanitized bucket is perfect.

3) Owners:
- Karthik (serving/runtime) will be the technical owner for standing up the dev pool and tuning batching/quantization.
- Grace (analytics) will own baseline dashboards, prompt evals, and the quality regression alert.
- Monica (SE) will run the success-criteria checks and the day-14 demo.

4) Prompt/eval plan: We’ll create an initial 50-prompt set covering short-form summarization, long-form summarization, and edge-case truncation. We’ll run a small manual eval to ensure outputs meet your quality bar before we scale the traffic.

5) Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: data residency/legal concerns — Mitigation: use sanitized non-prod bucket and document retention policy in MAP.
- Risk: burst behavior causing cold-start latency — Mitigation: we’ll provision warm dev pool capacity and autoscale thresholds tuned to your burst profile.

I’ve attached the updated MAP draft and the security questionnaire for your review. Can we lock 10am PT on 12/14 for kickoff? If so I’ll send a calendar invite with the agenda.

Thanks —
Monica
